task: get directions to a specific place with an online map (Google Maps, Apple Maps, Waze): search the destination, pick a travel mode, review the route options (time, tolls, transit lines), and start navigation or read off the chosen route; complete when the chosen route with its ETA is on screen or turn-by-turn navigation has begun. Surface pinned: the map product itself — not dashcam or driving footage, not travel vlogs that happen to show a map.

tree.label: Navigate to a destination
tree.note: do 1 - five keepers start in the phone's settings and two install the app first. 2 floats: before any destination when the preference is the point (zJVt, HrMd, 4AhB, mo0Q), through the per-route door from inside 4 (obk4, bQbE, kIU1, lYnD), or never. then 3, then 4 - except on desktop, where 4.1's form comes first and 3 happens inside it (7EYu, bQbE, 60tT). rework 4 until the route reads right. then one of three endings: 5 (sixteen keepers start guidance, none arrives on camera), 6 (keep or hand off the route instead - 7EYu, 60tT, ETAP, VO5N, sWXu), or nothing (bQbE, FfFy, HrMd, kIU1, PjID). 7 and 8 are excursions from the main map (PjID, QULM, aGGT); 7.5 reruns 3 and 4 offline.

children.label: Ready the device and app
children.note: 1.1 then 1.2 on a fresh install (1KTk, VO5N), with 1.3 where the store offers an update (QULM). 1.4 or 1.5 before the app ever opens - five keepers start at the OS level - and permission asks recur mid-task (5.2, 8.5). then 1.6, 1.7 where the platform asks, and 1.8 once the map is up. most keepers arrive with all of this already done and start at 1.6.

questions.question: Which app from the search results should you download?
questions.why: The search results show multiple options, including an ad for Google Maps, so you must verify you are tapping 'GET' on the correct Waze application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose which specific navigation app gets installed on your device.

questions.question: Do you confirm the installation of the Waze app?
questions.why: The screen shows an App Store prompt requiring Face ID or a double-click to authorize downloading Waze Navigation & Live Traffic.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the ability to personally authorize app downloads and manage your device's security.

questions.question: Do you want to review the app's ratings, privacy details, and specifications before downloading it?
questions.why: The screen displays a 4.8 rating, version history, and privacy information that can help verify the app's reliability and data usage before installation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally evaluate the app's trustworthiness and privacy practices based on user reviews and developer disclosures.

questions.question: Do you accept the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy to use the service?
questions.why: The screen explicitly states that using the service indicates your consent to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent blindly accept these agreements deprives you of knowing the specific data sharing and liability terms you are bound by.

questions.question: Should you allow the app to send you notifications?
questions.why: A system prompt asks if Waze can send notifications, which may include alerts, sounds, and icon badges.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over your device's privacy settings and whether the app is allowed to interrupt you with alerts.

questions.question: Do you want personalized ads based on your account info and app activity?
questions.why: The app asks if it can use your account information and activity to show personalized ads, which affects your data privacy.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might opt into personalized ads by default, sharing your personal data and app activity without your explicit consent.

questions.question: What level of location permission should you grant the app?
questions.why: The screen prompts you to choose between precise or approximate location access and how often the app can track you, which directly impacts both your privacy and the accuracy of the directions.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent decide means you lose the ability to enforce your own privacy boundaries regarding how and when your location data is shared.

questions.question: Are location services enabled and accessible to the Maps app?
questions.why: Verifying that the location toggle is on and Maps is listed under recent requests ensures the app can accurately determine your starting point for directions.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally audit your device's privacy settings and confirm exactly which apps have access to your location data.

questions.question: Should I sign in to your account before searching for the destination?
questions.why: The screen displays a menu with a 'Sign in' button and personalized features like 'Your timeline' and 'Location sharing' that become available if an account is linked.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting the agent decide whether to sign in means you lose control over whether your navigation data and location history are saved to your personal profile.

questions.question: Do you want to log into your account or continue as a guest?
questions.why: The onboarding screen offers a choice to log in or just get started, which determines if your saved places and preferences will be available.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to access your personalized account history and saved destinations for this trip.

questions.question: Is my current location accurate on the map before I get directions?
questions.why: Checking that the blue dot matches your actual surroundings ensures the app calculates the route from the correct starting point.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the physical awareness required to notice if the GPS has pinpointed the wrong starting location.

questions.question: Is the navigation screen stuck on a 'Searching for GPS' warning?
questions.why: If the device hasn't locked onto a GPS signal (often due to being indoors, in a city canyon, or in a parking garage), the initial turn-by-turn directions will be frozen or point in the wrong direction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to wait for a solid GPS lock before pulling into traffic, preventing you from making immediate wrong turns.
